title: Chicago Trivia Night

questions.q: The Great Chicago Fire broke out in which year?
Which Great Lake forms Chicago's eastern shoreline?
Name both of Chicago's Major League Baseball teams.
questions.a: The Cubs and the White Sox

questions.q: What is the name of the North Side ballpark famous for its ivy-covered outfield walls?
Every St. Patrick's Day, Chicago dyes what bright green?
The mirrored sculpture in Millennium Park known as "The Bean" has what official name?
Which condiment does Chicago tradition say must never go on a Chicago-style hot dog?
Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with which Chicago team?
Which ride, named after the engineer who built it, was the star attraction of Chicago's 1893 World's Columbian Exposition?
Chicago's Sears Tower was renamed in 2009. What is it called now?

notes: Began 8 October 1871; see Great Chicago Fire on Wikipedia or the Chicago History Museum.
See Chicago geography on Wikipedia or any map; the city sits on Lake Michigan's southwestern shore.
Cubs (National League) and White Sox (American League); see MLB.com team pages.
Wrigley Field ivy planted 1937; see Wrigley Field on Wikipedia or MLB.com/cubs.
Annual river dyeing since 1962; see Chicago St. Patrick's Day Parade site or Wikipedia.
Anish Kapoor sculpture, official title Cloud Gate; see City of Chicago Millennium Park page.
Standard toppings exclude ketchup by long-standing tradition; see Chicago-style hot dog on Wikipedia.
Bulls titles 1991-93 and 1996-98; see NBA.com or Michael Jordan on Wikipedia.
George Ferris's wheel at the 1893 fair; smaller wheels existed earlier, hence no 'debut' claim.
Renamed Willis Tower in July 2009; see Willis Tower on Wikipedia or willistower.com.
